source.title: From Flat Facts to Sharp Hallucinations: Detecting Stubborn Errors via Gradient Sensitivity
source.authors: Yee Zhing Liew; Andrew Huey Ping Tan; A. A. Abdul Majeed

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses sharpness and generalization theory, but its experiments test hallucination detection and compare sharpness between correct and incorrect answers; they do not test the listed train-test generalization claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own EPGS and Hessian-sharpness measurements, but does not measure training error, test error, or a training-test gap. Those measurements are recorded under fits_no_version and are not evidence for V7.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization connection to motivate hallucination detection. Its own results measure detection performance and per-example curvature in fixed pretrained LLMs, not magnitude-aware sharpness versus training–test gaps across trained networks. None of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that EPGS provides an efficient proxy for Hessian sharpness and detects high-confidence factual errors across evaluated open-weight LLMs. They interpret this as distinguishing flat factual knowledge from sharp memorized errors; that interpretation does not constitute a test of V7.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates pretrained LLMs for hallucination detection; it does not use a training recipe that tests the listed generalization claims.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported EPGS detection performance varies with dataset labeling criterion and with gradient extraction location, perturbation magnitude, entity masking, and decoding temperature.

fits_no_version.finding: For Llama-3-8B on 50 robust facts and 50 stubborn hallucinations from TriviaQA, EPGS correlated with the top Hessian eigenvalue (Pearson r = 0.855; p < 10−28; Spearman ρ = 0.862). Stubborn hallucinations had a 2.5× larger average eigenvalue.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within this sampled checkpoint and dataset, EPGS tracks per-example Hessian curvature, and high-confidence factual errors have greater average curvature than robust facts. This does not establish a relationship with training–test generalization gaps.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The paper's evidence concerns hallucination detection rather than training-test generalization. The direct Hessian comparison uses 50 examples per category from one dataset and one model; the reported correlation does not measure generalization gaps.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under matched training recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier test error and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover held-out performance.
Training-time dropout effects on held-out classification error. Inference-time dropout is evaluated only as a hallucination-detection perturbation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance versus training–test gaps across comparably fitted convolutional networks, including ranking against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Section E.2 explicitly frames sharpness as a differential diagnostic within fixed checkpoints. Detection AUROC, inference-time dropout comparisons, and cited reparameterization arguments supply no additional tests of the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness tracks the training-test gap.
Whether removing memorized training examples lowers test accuracy.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared EPGS score with top Hessian eigenvalue for robust facts and stubborn hallucinations.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between EPGS score and true Hessian sharpness
rows.note: This is a correlation with hallucination class-related sharpness, not with a training-test generalization gap.
rows.check: The reported r = 0.855 and p < 10−28 match Appendix C.1. Correlation between EPGS and a Hessian eigenvalue does not measure any claim version.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared average top Hessian eigenvalue for stubborn hallucinations with robust facts.
rows.note: The comparison concerns factual correctness categories, not training and test errors.
rows.check: The 2.5× average eigenvalue ratio matches Appendix C.1. This compares incorrect and correct predictions within one checkpoint, rather than generalization gaps across networks; it does not test V7.
